text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
CanParticipate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
USCitizen(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
TaiwaneseCitizen(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
RussianOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.

Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → CanParticipate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (USCitizen(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (USCitizen(x) ⊕ TaiwaneseCitizen(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
∀x (RussianOfficial(x) → ¬TaiwaneseCitizen(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬TaiwaneseCitizen(vladimir) ∧ ¬ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(ekaterina) ∨ RussianOfficial(ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.

Conclusion:
CanParticipate(ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(vladimir) ::: Ekaterina can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election or Vladimir is a manager at Gazprom.
